name: The five stages of the Pāśupata path (avasthā-pañcaka)

stages.name: vyakta (manifest)
stages.gloss: the stage in which the Pāśupata sign is shown
stages.description: After initiation the brahmin lives in the temple under his teacher, bathes and lies in ash, wears the used garland, worships with laughter, song, dance, the ḍuṇḍuṅ sound, prostration and muttering, keeps the ten restraints and lives on alms. Place: the teacher. Gain: knowledge. Purification: removal of turbidity.
stages.ref: GK 5-7; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 2, 5, 6; PS 1.2-1.17; PABh on PS 5.29

stages.name: avyakta (unmanifest)
stages.gloss: the stage in which sign and learning are hidden
stages.description: With the teacher's leave, having gained knowledge, he goes among people with his sign hidden and courts dishonour by feigned sleep, trembling, limping, amorous gestures, senseless acts and speech, and by wandering like a madman on discarded food; revilers take his demerit and give him their merit. Place: people. Gain: austerity (the whole of dharma).
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5; PS 3.1-4.18; PABh on PS 3.12-17, 5.29

stages.name: jaya (conquest)
stages.gloss: the stage of conquering the senses
stages.description: In an empty house or cave he conquers the senses, recites the chosen Gāyatrī, meditates on Oṃ with fixation in the heart and remains constantly with the god; after six months of constant yoga the powers arise in abundance. Place: cave. Gain: constant union with the god.
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5; PS 5.1-25; PABh on PS 5.13, 5.29

stages.name: cheda (cutting)
stages.gloss: the stage ending in the cutting [of bonds]
stages.description: He lives in the cremation ground until the body falls, on whatever comes, always remembering Rudra; he attains union with Rudra. Place: cremation ground. Gain: steadiness / union.
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5, 6; PS 5.30-34; PABh on PS 5.29

stages.name: niṣṭhā (completion)
stages.gloss: the stage in which all activity has ceased
stages.description: All the practitioner's activity has ceased; without body, his place is Rudra alone; having cut the root of the faults and fixed the mind on Rudra, vigilant, he reaches the end of sufferings by the Lord's grace and does not return. Gain: perfection (the Lord's qualities).

notes: Stage names from the Gaṇakārikā; Kauṇḍinya gives the same progression through residence, livelihood, strength, action, purification and gain. Initiation (B0) precedes stage 1. Bands are interpretation-layer claims: the first two stages are ascetic-ritual preparation (B2), conquest of the senses in solitude is withdrawal and concentration (B3, with absorption and powers as it matures), the cremation-ground stage is deepening after the powers (B6), completion is final liberation (B7). The Ratnaṭīkā rejects a separate 'stage of the perfected'.
